```{r}
#| label: load-packages
#| include: false

library(ggplot2) # For making data viz
library(readxl) # Reading data in from Excel
library(dplyr) # Data manipulation
library(forcats) # Factor reordering
library(lubridate) # Working with dates
library(janitor) # cleaning functions, e.g. cleaning names
library(ggcorrplot) # visualizing correlation matrices
library(broom) # Produces tidy output for tables
library(gt)
```

```{r}
#| label: load-data
#| include: false

fd <- read_xlsx("clothes_expend.xlsx", sheet = "clothes_expend") |> 
  clean_names()
```

## Instructions

For questions 1 - 9, you will follow along with Ryan and insert the data visualizations into this Quarto document. You will use the `clothes_expend.xlsx` file located on Canvas to generate the figures. We will work in an `.R` file and transfer our code to this Quarto document for submission in Canvas. You will have to solve problem 10 and 11 on your own or with friends. 

1. Compute a histogram for `price_index`. How would you describe the distribution? 

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false


p <- ggplot(data = fd,
            aes(x = price_index))
p + geom_histogram(col = "gold", fill = "maroon") +
  labs(x = "Price Index") + 
  theme_minimal()
```


2. Using the same variable as in 1, add a density plot to the histogram. 

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
p + geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), 
                   col = "gold", fill = "maroon") +
  geom_density(fill = "navy", alpha = .5, col = "lightblue") +
  labs(x = "Price Index") + 
  theme_minimal()
```


3. Compute summary statistics for `price_index`. 

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
p <- ggplot(data = fd,
            aes(y = sales_index, x = realgdp_b))

p + geom_point(alpha = .5) +
  geom_smooth() + # method = "lm" adds the linear reg line
  labs(x = "Real GDP",
       y = "Sales Index") +
  theme_minimal()
```


4. Compute the mean and standard deviation of `price_index`. 

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
summary(fd$price_index)
```


5. Compute additional summary statistics for all variables

```{r}
summary(fd)
```


6. Produce a correlation matrix for the `clothes_expend` data set. What variable seems to be the most correlated with `sales_index`, excluding `sales_b`?

```{r}
cor(fd)
```


7. This is a little hard to visualize, so let's try creating a nice visualization using the `ggcorrplot` package (Note: Install it if it's not installed.)

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
cor_mat <- cor(fd)
ggcorrplot(cor_mat, hc.order = TRUE, type = "upper", method = "circle")

p <- ggplot(data = fd,
            aes(y = sales_index, x = realgdp_b))

```

10. Repeat 1-4 using the `sales_index` variable. Comment on your findings. 
```{r}
p <- ggplot(data = fd,
            aes(x = sales_index))
p + geom_histogram(col = "gold", fill = "maroon") +
  labs(x = "Sales Index") + 
  theme_minimal()
p + geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), 
                   col = "gold", fill = "maroon") +
  geom_density(fill = "navy", alpha = .5, col = "lightblue") +
  labs(x = "Sales Index") + 
  theme_minimal()
p <- ggplot(data = fd,
            aes(y = sales_index, x = realgdp_b))

p + geom_point(alpha = .5) +
  geom_smooth() + # method = "lm" adds the linear reg line
  labs(x = "Real GDP",
       y = "Sales Index") +
  theme_minimal()

summary(fd$sales_index)

```
